title: money as magical transit map
content:
transforming money systems into creative play

while doing my taxes this year (and in the process, making this tax therapy t-rex microbook), I felt exhausted and depleted in dealing with the cold language of IRS income/expenses/deductibles/blah, so I made up my own metaphorical systems and lexicon to think about and relate to money, in an imaginative and playful way — money as an integrated transit system.

transforming the discomfort of money

but first, why, you ask?

because I can’t work with — or transform something — if I don’t want to look at it. if I want to nurture my business and financial infrastructure, I need to call it something other than “financial infrastructure.” I need to come up with creative ways to deal with what can feel like a sticky, complicated, entangled, anxiety-inducing sore subject — (not because money is by definition hard or sore or evil, but because of our cultural conditioning and disempowering programming around it).

I know that if I want to grow my business, I need to treat my business as its own creative form — and, therefore, money as an expression and extension of my creative energy.

I’ve been circling around the topic of money a lot the last years — as I recounciled the tension between artist/entrepreneur, and the truth that money is a mirror and derivative of creative energy, not its mortal enemy.

here’s my metaphor:

money systems are like an interconnected transit system — where money is the passenger.

money systems: flow & containers

the purpose of a transit system is to keep all passengers (or cargo) in motion — going to the right places — at the right times. transit systems contain interconnected components: if one part experience failures or delays, it will ripple out and affect the entire system. I write more about interconnected systems here.

the purpose of all money structures is to move money around — let’s call this movement flow. you can also call it “channels.” it requires different kinds of flow —

  • incoming flow (income)

  • transition flow (movement between spaces)

  • outgoing flow (spending)

flow is always going somewhere. therefore, all flow requires vessels/containers — holding spaces. this is usually a bank or financial institution of some sort.

a business — as an interconnected system of parts — is about moving money flow through pathways or channels — into specific vessels/containers.

and, as I’ve written about previously, even money is just the byproduct or derivative of creative flow — or our channeling of energy, time, resources, inspiration, experience — into different offerings that represent the distillation of our wisdom and gifts for others to experience. it’s about sharing our creative resources with the world, and receiving resoruces for it, in turn.


the transit system metaphor

I’ll explain how all of this applies in my metaphor — to find more clarity and ease in your “financial infrastructures,” or containers for your money flow.

first, money arrives as incoming flights

perhaps your different business offerings represent different airlines, or flight paths. some of them arrive consistently, every week or month. others are more unpredictable.

if you wanted to grow your income, it’s about looking at your current flights (income sources), their relative frequency, and which flights to channel more energy into. or, which new flight paths you want to open.

your offerings are literally journeys.
your business is the airport.

money goes to your business bank (central station)

one way or other — whether you use a payment processer (like stripe, venmo, paypal) or not, all incoming flows (ideally) would be connected, via transit, to your business bank.

I’m calling this “central station,” like a train station. at this station, there’s two holding spaces —

  • government lounge (aka, savings for taxes)

  • business lounge (savings for your business) — which would be used to pay business expenses.


money flows to your personal bank (home station)

after some money passengers go to your two waiting lounges, the others go to your personal bank, which I’m calling “home station.” at home station, a portion of your money might be directed into other holding containers

  • the weather dome — savings for rainy or thunderstorm-y days

  • port of future dreams — savings for future plans

the rest of your money would be used to power pathways — like subway or bus routes — for your day to day life. these pathways represent your channeling of resources into different domains of your life: groceries, rent, utilities, etc etc.

a structural map to work towards

I will unbashfully admit that my business and personal money structures / transit systems are nowhere as clear and organized as the model I outlined, above. there’s missing transits, missing stops, missing containers. I am, personally, extremely avoidant when it comes at doing this kind of business admin-y things — it used to fill me with great anxiety and dread, and would leave me absolutely wiped out, afterwards.

hence, my imaginative metaphorical map — is my solution to all that.

it’s not my current reality; it’s my map for what I am working towards.

airports that feel like magical botanical gardens.

waiting lounges filled with an abundance of resources.

passenger flights that nourish my entire ecosystem — and ripple far beyond.

I have big dreams for my transit system — to make it green, sustainable, magical. consider this image my initial, version 1.0 blueprint. I’ll be moving toward it in tiny circles and small, incremental steps. then I’ll be transforming and evolving it, again.
